subject.title: [Bug]: cron.remove does not clean up session records in sessions.json

question: Should deleted cron jobs purge their base session record immediately on `cron.remove`, or should orphaned base sessions only be reaped later through `cron.sessionRetention`?
rationale: Current source leaves base cron session rows untouched, while linked retention work preserves live base rows because they can carry model/auth/label state; choosing immediate deletion versus retention-based orphan cleanup needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Ownership-Aware Immediate Purge
options.body: Make `cron.remove` remove only the deleted job's owned base/session artifacts and any current run-history remnants, with regression coverage proving active jobs' base rows are preserved.

options.title: Retention-Only Orphan Cleanup
options.body: Keep `cron.remove` limited to job config and rely on the reaper to prune stale orphaned base rows after the configured retention window.

options.title: Close After Broader Retention Fix
options.body: Treat the ghost-session case as part of the broader cron session retention work and close this only after that path lands with explicit deleted-job coverage.

recommendation.title: Ownership-Aware Immediate Purge
recommendation.body: Make `cron.remove` remove only the deleted job's owned base/session artifacts and any current run-history remnants, with regression coverage proving active jobs' base rows are preserved.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and adjacent cron/session refactor history make this the best available routing owner for the lifecycle-policy choice.
